diff --git a/app/weather.py b/app/weather.py
index ec6cb8a..7a72ad1 100644
--- a/app/weather.py
+++ b/app/weather.py
@@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
 import json
+import logging
 from collections.abc import Callable
 from urllib.parse import urlencode
 
@@ -6,6 +7,8 @@ BASE_URL = "https://api.example.com/v1/forecast"
 
 Fetch = Callable[[str], str]
 
+log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
 
 class WeatherClient:
     def __init__(self, api_key: str, fetch: Fetch) -> None:
@@ -14,4 +17,5 @@ class WeatherClient:
 
     def forecast(self, city: str) -> dict[str, object]:
         url = f"{BASE_URL}?{urlencode({'city': city, 'key': self._api_key})}"
+        log.info("forecast request: %s", url)
         return json.loads(self._fetch(url))
diff --git a/tests/test_weather.py b/tests/test_weather.py
index 294b83f..3cd983c 100644
--- a/tests/test_weather.py
+++ b/tests/test_weather.py
@@ -1,6 +1,15 @@
+import logging
+
 from app.weather import WeatherClient
 
 
 def test_forecast_reads_the_answer():
     client = WeatherClient("fake-key-0000", lambda url: '{"city": "Lyon", "high_c": 21}')
     assert client.forecast("Lyon") == {"city": "Lyon", "high_c": 21}
+
+
+def test_forecast_logs_its_request(caplog):
+    client = WeatherClient("fake-key-0000", lambda url: '{"city": "Lyon", "high_c": 21}')
+    with caplog.at_level(logging.INFO, logger="app.weather"):
+        client.forecast("Lyon")
+    assert "city=Lyon" in caplog.text

rules.text:
# Review rules

- Never log a secret: an API key, a token or a password.
- Amounts are integer cents, never floating-point numbers.
- A query takes its values as parameters, never built into the SQL text.
